messages:
mike: Quick FYI - I started a microbenchmark sweep after the QKV packing + bias+rope epilogue fusion landed and seeing a surprising regression on long sequences (L=2048).
mike: Numbers: baseline fused-attn (no pack) = 86 ms/token, packed+epilogue-fuse = 115 ms/token on A100 (p4d). ~33% slower.
anika: ouch. Was the batch size or KV cache mode different?
mike: same bench harness, bs=1, beam=1, kv-cache enabled. I re-ran with paged-attn off and still see slowdown.
sara: can you paste the exact nvprof/nsys command and kernel timeline? prefer a short trace not full profile.
mike: sure. ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o /tmp/trace` then `python -m bench.attn --model gpt2-xl --seq 2048 --config packed_epilogue`.

mike: kernel timeline excerpt:
```
FlashFusedAttn_pack_qkv<<<...>>>  time=2.1ms  (high occupancy)
FlashFusedAttn_epilogue<<<...>>> time=3.9ms  (regression)
FlashFusedAttn_unpacked_epilogue<<<...>>> time=2.2ms (baseline)
```

liam: epilogue almost doubled. Could be register spilling from additional math (bias + rope) fused in epilogue causing lower SM utilization.
liam: also check shared memory usage; packing may change alignment so epilogue does uncoalesced stores.

anika: good call. mike, can you run with `cuobjdump --dump-ptx` for the epilogue kernel and `cuMemGetInfo` traces? also add `-Xptxas -v` to nvcc for compiler regcounts if building locally.

mike: attached quick diff of regcount from local build: epilogue before fusion = 54 regs, after fusion = 78 regs.
perf-bot: automated note: elevated register pressure often lowers occupancy and can increase latency; see KB-1021.

sara: If regcount jump is real we may need to split epilogue into two-stage: bias/rope precompute into a small kernel then a light-weight store kernel. That keeps fused compute smaller.

anika: alternatively try selective fusion: allow qkv pack + bias fusion but skip rope in epilogue for long-seq codepath. We already have heuristics for seq>1024 in batch chooser.

mike: I'll run two quick experiments: 1) selective-rope-off when seq>1024; 2) two-stage epilogue (precompute then write). Expect results in ~2 hours.

liam: also add microbench with different cache modes: KV cached vs streaming (paged). There was an odd interaction earlier where paged attention made epilogue do extra indexing.

mike: noted. filing perf ticket with logs and nvprof: https://redwood/issue/INF-2984 (will link traces). assigning to eng-runtime/attn-kernels.

sara: thanks. once you have the two experiment numbers, we can decide if we revert the fusion for long seq or add heuristics in kernel chooser.

mike: will update here. :thumbsup:
